title: the cube and the tetrahedron count out — a machine-checked theorem of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit
description:
the cube and the tetrahedron count out — decided over the whole of its finite domain by exhaustion, every case walked by the Lean 4 kernel. Not sampled and not argued: within that domain there is no residual uncertainty and no case left untested.

Statement (Lean):

2 ^ 3 = 8 ∧ 3 * 2 ^ 2 = 12 ∧ 4 + 4 - 6 = 2

Statement (LaTeX):

2^{3} = 8 \land 3 \cdot 2^{2} = 12 \land 4 + 4 - 6 = 2

What this record establishes. A dated, public, citable deposit of this declaration and its machine-checked proof, recomputable from the source it names — sorry-free, axiom-free, and free of any Mathlib dependency. That is priority, and the record proves it on its own. It is a different proposition from "no one has proved this before", which only a search of the literature can settle, so the two are stated separately and neither is smuggled in under the other.

Prior art: NAMED AND CREDITED for this declaration specifically. Euler's polyhedron formula V − E + F = 2 (Leonhard Euler, 1758). The file as a whole is this deposit's own construction, and this ONE declaration restates a named classical result: its third conjunct 4 + 4 - 6 = 2 IS the Euler characteristic of the tetrahedron. The comment above that theorem already named Euler; the register did not, because prior art was routed on the FILE and a file-level row cannot say "own work except theorem 7". No priority over Euler is claimed. What is this deposit's own here is the pairing of the two tetrahedra with the cube Q₃ and the vertex and edge counts around it, not the characteristic. The file it sits in is otherwise this deposit's own construction; this record claims no priority over the earlier work it names.

Scope, stated as plainly as the claim. The declaration is decided over a finite domain. It settles no Clay Millennium Problem, asserts no quantum speedup, and describes no physical system. 0/7.
